data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's central transfer claim — that a non-zero baseline of isolated, diverse failures is a *signal* of structural independence and that a 'too quiet' redundant system is *more likely* to mask a hidden common-cause vulnerability — inverts the evidential logic the problem asks about. The problem requires identifying evidence that distinguishes genuinely independent failures from merely-uncorrelated-until-shared-cause failures. But a steady stream of isolated failures is itself compatible with a shared latent cause that is partially triggered (e.g., a common library bug that manifests stochastically across nodes under varying load). SRC_001 treats the 'noise' as positive evidence of independence without specifying any causal test that would separate noisy-but-independent from noisy-but-shared-cause. In doing so it confuses a description of the failure pattern with evidence of its causal origin — the very conflation the problem asks to resolve.
